answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and thus it burns the thread fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the umber ledger attributes every share, the river audit publishes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 72% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not burn. That is 25 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
